chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: Drinking on the job and a drummer's habits
summary: The band rarely drank on the job; Ramey tells about a drummer drunk afternoons and nights and his marriage.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: What'd you do in the 40 minutes?
Well, you know, in Kansas City, Missouri we had a dressing room we went to.
We very seldom would drink on the job, you know. I think when we finally got Bird, he may have goofed a little hit. But everybody pretty much was a gentleman, and took care of the job pretty good.
Do you feel in a job like that 40 minutes off is a long time sitting around. But I suppose you --
Yeah, but we were so -- I imagine some of us drank, but it wasn't anything ever noticeable, at all. Because naturally, we were trying to protect that job. Nobody --
And Jo Jones wasn't drinking too heavily then?
No. One thing before, when I knew him, you'd see him drunk in the afternoon, like that.

Yeah, he'd go out to some of the bars on the corners, something, with all the guys. And when he was on his way down there to the band, Lee (Stuart) or whoever it was he was working with at the Reno, you'd see him already tore up, you know.

But then he started taking care of business. He would get drunk, you know: by the time we would leave he'd started getting drunk, you know. And then when we'd get down on 18th Street and Vine, you know, where the gang is, he'd get tore up. And I'd have to take him home.
Well, when did he get married, then?
He was already married when he came to Kansas City. He was married to a girl named Abbie C. (PHONETIC).
